To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bioinformatics enrichment tools can be classified into three categories: over-representation analysis, gene set enrichment analysis and network-based analysis.

(a) the majority of tools are based on the gene-set overrepresentation (GSO) algorithm and the hypergeometric distribution (HG) test; (b) the gene-set over- and under-representation (GSOR) algorithm is used in only a few tools; and (c) the gene-set enrichment (GSE) algorithm is used only in a few tools that are not widely adopted.

(1) gene-annotation enrichment tools have been developed for the functional analysis of large lists of genes, (2) these tools can be categorized into three major categories according to the enrichment algorithms they use and (3) each tool category has unique advantages and disadvantages.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of bioinformatics enrichment tools, which are used to identify the most important biological processes and molecular functions associated with large gene lists.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current enrichment tools have made a great contribution to the functional analysis of gene lists.
the gene-annotation enrichment tools are a valuable and powerful tool for investigators to identify biologically relevant pathways and gene sets in a large gene list.

the bioinformatics enrichment tool survey provides a unique, systematic and up-to-date overview of the current state of the art of gene-annotation enrichment tools, which will facilitate the design, development and use of these tools.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many tools available for gene set enrichment analysis, and that the tools are categorized by their algorithmic approaches.
, although the bioinformatics enrichment tools are becoming increasingly popular, the majority of them are still at their infancy and are far from being a mature technology.
